issues.detail: The Hebrew 'בָּמוֹת הַבַּעַל' means 'high places of Baal' (בַּעַל = Baal, the deity). The Chinese renders it as '主人的高處' ('high places of the master/lord'), which loses the proper name 'Baal' and substitutes a generic title. This changes the referent from the specific deity Baal to a generic 'master,' which is a substantive meaning change.
